title: Session-context-and-multi-hop-tracing-playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for instrumenting, sampling, and dashboarding multi-hop traces that carry session context through Redwood's inference stack. Focus is on the common end-to-end flow: API gateway -> router -> frontend cache layer -> serving runtime -> model shard / variant -> fallback routing -> response assemble. Goal: make it easy to answer questions like:
  - Which requests experienced a model-variant fallback and why?
  - How often did KV cache prefixes avoid full re-eval?
  - How many inferences were part of the same logical session and did session affinity affect latency?

It's intentionally pragmatic: example span layouts, attribute names, sampling heuristics, query snippets, dashboard widget ideas, and incident triage steps.

Definitions (key concepts)

- session_id: short identifier attached to a user session or conversational context. Not PII. Used strictly for grouping traces/metrics (hashed if necessary).
- request_id: unique per-API-call (UUID). Primary trace id if propagated.
- correlation_id: used when a single user request fans out to multiple internal requests (e.g., re-ranker + generator).
- hop: any network/service boundary that creates a span (gateway, router, cache, runtime, model-worker).
- multi-hop trace: a trace with >1 service/hop.

Recommended span model (flat + semantic roles)

We prefer a small set of span kinds rather than deeply nested arbitrary spans. Keep span names consistent across services to enable simple queries.

Span attributes (recommended keys)

- span.name: human-friendly (e.g., api.gateway.request, router.route, cache.kv.lookup, runtime.infer, model.worker.exec)
- request_id: string
- session_id: string(hashed)
- user_tier: free|paid|enterprise
- model_name: e.g., redwood-7b-q4f16
- model_variant: fp16|q4_0|q4_1
- shard_id: worker-17
- kv_cache_hit: true|false
- kv_prefix_len: int (tokens)
- token_length: int (token count requested)
- output_tokens: int (tokens generated)
- batch_size: int
- routed_reason: capacity|latency_sla|region|fallback_policy
- fallback_triggered: boolean
- fallback_target: model_name if fallback occurred
- latency_ms: float (span duration in ms)
- error: boolean
- error_kind: e.g., oom|rpc_timeout|invalid_input

Span naming and examples

- api.gateway.request: initial HTTP/GRPC entry span (contains http metadata, request_id, session_id)
- router.route: decision span (shows model target, variant selected, reason)
- cache.kv.lookup: prefix/KV cache probe (attrs: kv_cache_hit, kv_prefix_len)
- runtime.batch.exec: runtime execution for a batch (attrs: batch_size, shard_id, model_variant)
- model.worker.exec: low-level worker span for token generation (attrs: output_tokens, token_length)
- response.assemble: any postprocessing, rerank, or tool-calling assembly

Sampling strategy (practical, tiered, and context-aware)

We cannot afford full tracing at 100% for hosted traffic. Sampling must preserve critical classes for debugging while keeping costs bounded. Proposed rules: 

1) Deterministic keep for error traces: keep 100% when error=true at any span.
2) Session-based reservoir: keep the first trace for a session_id per minute at higher sampling (10%) to build session-level timelines.
3) High-value tiers: enterprise customer requests: 25% baseline sample.
4) Fallbacks & cache-miss amplification: if router.route.fallback_triggered==true OR cache.kv_lookup.kv_cache_hit==false then increase sampling weight (to 50% or 100% for enterprise).
5) Tail latency amplification: any trace where runtime.batch.exec latency_ms > p99_threshold -> sample with higher probability for 30 minutes for same session_id.

Implementation notes:
- Use client-side deterministic sampling keyed on hashed(session_id + minute) to get reproducible sampling decisions across services for low-overhead gating.
- Emit a sampling_decision attribute on root span for clarity in dashboards.

Metric definitions (naming conventions and metrics to create)

Naming: metrics should be prefixed to group by product: inference.<component>.<metric> or obs.<component>.<metric>. Use tagset to filter (model_name, model_variant, user_tier, region).

Core counters and gauges (examples):

- inference.requests_total (counter) tags: model_name, user_tier, region, session_bucket
  Description: total number of top-level inference requests received.

- inference.kv_cache_hits_total (counter) tags: model_name, kv_prefix_len_bucket
  Description: count of prefix cache hits. Consider incrementing a separate counter for partial hits (soft hits) if present.

- inference.fallbacks_total (counter) tags: from_variant, to_variant, reason
  Description: how often router chooses fallback variants.

- inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 (histogram or summary) tags: model_name, model_variant, user_tier
  Description: end-to-end request latency.

- runtime.batch.size_histogram (histogram) tags: model_name, shard_id
  Description: distribution of runtime batch sizes.

- runtime.oom_count (counter) tags: shard_id, model_name
  Description: OOMs observed on workers.

- session.active_count (gauge) tags: user_tier
  Description: number of active sessions in last N minutes (derived via cardinality of session_id with TTL).

Derived metrics and useful slices

- kv_cache_effectiveness = inference.kv_cache_hits_total / inference.requests_total (by model_name)
- fallback_rate = inference.fallbacks_total / inference.requests_total
- p99_tail_risk = fraction of requests with runtime.batch.exec latency > 3x median

Example queries (PromQL-like pseudocode)

- kv cache hit rate (1h): sum(inference_kv_cache_hits_total{model_name="redwood-7b"}) / sum(inference_requests_total{model_name="redwood-7b"})

- fallbacks by reason (24h): topk(10, sum(inference_fallbacks_total) by (reason))

- tail latency heatmap (tokens vs latency): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, token_length))

Dashboard widgets and layout (practical set)

Top row (operator summary)
- Global RPS (by user_tier)
- 95/99 latency for critical endpoints (three small sparklines by model_name)
- Active sessions (gauge with trend)

Second row (routing and cache health)
- KV cache hit rate (timeseries) with model_name filter and kv_prefix_len breakdown (stacked)
- Fallback rate by variant (bar)
- Router decision funnel: requests -> cache probes -> runtime execs -> fallbacks (single stacked bar with counts)

Third row (runtime and tail risk)
- Batch size distribution (histogram)
- Runtime p99 latency heatmap by token_length (x-axis token_length buckets, y-axis latency bins)
- OOMs and worker errors (timeseries and table of top shards)

Trace exploration quick-links

- Saved trace filter: fallback_triggered:true AND kv_cache_hit:false (to find worst-case re-eval flows)
- Saved trace filter: runtime.batch.exec.latency_ms > 2000 (p99 tail)
- Session timeline link: session_id={{session_id}} -> show traces for that session for last 10 minutes

Incident triage playbook (short)

1) Symptom: sudden spike in p99 latency for a model
  - Check runtime.batch.exec p99 and batch_size distribution. If batch_size fell to 1 while RPS stayed similar, root cause could be batching regression in router.
  - Check kv_cache_hit trend. If hits dropped, more full evals may be increasing latency.
  - Check fallback_rate. If increased, fallbacks to slower variant may be the cause.
  - Use trace filters for high-latency traces to find whether latency is concentrated in model.worker.exec or network hops.

2) Symptom: increase in errors/ooms
  - Inspect runtime.oom_count by shard_id. Pull model.worker.exec spans for failed traces to see memory footprint hints (batch_size, token_length).

3) Symptom: user complaint about conversation state missing
  - Look up session_id, query traces across router and cache.kv.lookup spans to see whether cache writes were performed, whether TTL evictions occurred, or whether a fallback to a model variant caused state drift.

Ownership and rollout plan

- Phase 1 (0-2 weeks): instrument all spans with the attribute set above in a canary service (router + runtime). Emit metrics for requests_total, kv_cache_hits_total, inference_latency buckets.
- Phase 2 (2-6 weeks): implement deterministic sampling logic and amplify sampling for fallbacks and errors. Create the initial dashboard and saved trace filters.
- Phase 3 (6-12 weeks): onboard additional services, refine alerts and alerts-to-SLO mapping, iterate on tag cardinality reduction (bucket model_name and kv_prefix_len).

Open questions / trade-offs (to resolve)

- session_id privacy: should we hash client-provided identifiers by default or only when requested by privacy team?
- tag cardinality: model_name has many variants — agree on a mapping table to reduce cardinality in dashboards (e.g., group by model_family).
- KV cache metrics: do we want to expose partial hits as a separate metric or encode as kv_prefix_len buckets?

Notes to reviewers

- This is targeted at engineers implementing traces and dashboard owners who will maintain alerts. Please add concrete PromQL/Datadog queries you rely on, and any objections to attribute names (we'll keep them stable — changing is expensive once queries exist).

Scratchpad / quick checks

- Are we emitting session_id on client SDKs? - TODO: devx/SDKs to confirm.
- Add a saved dashboard link to the router runbook once this doc lands.

References and related docs

- tracing-sampling-and-span-design-for-tokenized-inference (existing) — complements this by deeper sampling proofs.
- telemetry-prioritization-runbook-inference-sli-mapping (existing)

End of playbook (working draft)
